newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates De Nationale Investeringsbank.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates De Nationale Investeringsbank.

text.p: IBCA said on Monday it assigned a long-term rating of AA to the Dutch credit institution De Nationale Investeringsbank.
IBCA also sid in a statement that it had assigned short-term, individual and legal ratings of A1 plus, B and 2 respectively.
De Nationale Investeringsbank (DNIB) is 50.3 percent owned by the Dutch state, ith the remainder held by Dutch insitutional and retail investors, IBCA said.
"DNIB's asset quality is sound, reflecting the strength of the Dutch economy and the quality of the bank's credit research," it said.

"Profitability has been stable because of the bank's reliance on interest income, and performance ratios compare well with those of the major Dutch banks despite its conservative market risk policies."
IBCA said the bank was very liquid and had a well diversified funding base of Dutch and international institutional investors.
It said DNIB was well capitalised and had a total capital/weighted risks ratio of nearly 15 percent at end-June 1996.

DNIB is a wholesale bank specialising, directly and through subsidiaries, in long-term lending, asset and project finance, equity investments, capital market transactions, financial consultancy and brokerage activities.
